meta.title: Keep connector C: redesign it now, fix bundle service, and decide any 2029 sunset on evidence
meta.subtitle: Board question: should Vesper discontinue low reported-margin sterile connector C and redeploy the team to connector D? Pre-read for the February 2027 board meeting
meta.purpose: Decide whether to discontinue connector C and redeploy the team to connector D
meta.confidentiality: Synthetic benchmark data · US$ millions, FY2026 full year, from the board briefing pack

inputs.label: Finished analysis deck, extracted slide by slide

storyline.governing_thought: Do not discontinue C in 2027: exiting destroys cash and breaches board constraints. Redesign C, fix bundle service and make any sunset a 2029 decision

exec_summary.text: C's 8% margin comes from the cost allocation; on contribution margin, C is actually the portfolio's strongest connector

sub_points.text: C earns $3.8M of direct contribution, a 63% margin, compared with 50% for D and A and 42% for B
Only $0.4M of C's $3.3M allocated cost is avoidable; the other $2.9M would move onto A, B and D

exec_summary.text: Exiting C in 2027 loses $4.75M in the first year and $2.65M every year after, and breaks two non-negotiables

sub_points.text: Even at the optimistic 25% migration D adds only $0.75M; break-even needs $6.8M of D sales (113% of C)
The $2.1M penalty alone is 2.3 times the $0.9M envelope; C is in 9 of 14 major bundles, with no validated substitute

exec_summary.text: The customer case for exit does not hold up: the real problem is bundle fill, caused by A and B

sub_points.text: The 9-percentage-point renewal gap is confounded by size, equipment and coverage, with no before/after test
C's 98% on-time figure omits A/B bundle misses; bundle fill is 91% against 95%, and exit would not fix it

exec_summary.text: Recommended: redesign C now (+$2.4M over 2027–29), recover bundle fill, then hand the team to D

sub_points.text: The $0.55M redesign pays back in about 5 months, breaks even at 19% of the saving and fits the $0.9M
Renew the two bundles without exit notice, with a consent-based D path; Q4 2028 gate on any 2029 sunset

next_steps.action: Take the six decisions: reject a 2027 exit, approve the $0.55M redesign and $0.35M reserve, mandate the bundle-fill KPI, set Gate 2 criteria
Set renewal terms for the two bundles: C retained, consent-based D clause, 2029-aligned term
Present the A/B bundle-fill recovery plan to reach ≥95%, with dates and cost
Run the C redesign and two-site pilot; bring Gate 1 (convert the whole line?) to the board
Run D adapter qualification with willing C customers and record observed acceptance
Gate 2: decide any 2029 sunset on observed evidence, before contract notice deadlines

lead_message.text: Our starting hypothesis, "keep C", survived four of five tests; the fifth showed that keeping C unchanged is not enough

slides.rationale: Five tests of one hypothesis on the same three attributes -> comparison table with a verdict column
slides.unit_line: **Initial hypothesis, set before testing:** retain C, because its low reported margin is an allocation effect rather than an avoidable economic cost

rows.label: 1. C earns more cash than its exit would save

cells.text: $3.8M direct contribution against $0.4M avoidable fixed cost: exit gives up a net $3.4M a year before migration

rows.label: 2. D cannot replace what C earns

cells.text: Ceiling of 25% of C revenue = $1.5M (all of D's spare capacity) × 50% = $0.75M, against $3.4M at stake
$2.1M first-year penalties against $0.9M approved cash; C in 9 of 14 major bundles; no substitute validated on every hospital model

rows.label: 4. C is not driving customer attrition

cells.text: 9-percentage-point renewal gap is correlational and confounded (size, legacy equipment, coverage); no before/after evidence
Bundle fill 91% against 95% required; C faces price pressure; a $1.25M a year redesign saving costs $0.55M

callout.detail: Revised answer: keep C, but not unchanged. Fund the redesign, restore 95% bundle fill, use the renewals to open a consent-based path to D, and decide any 2029 sunset in Q4 2028 on observed evidence

footnotes: Test 4 stays open, and the plan includes a way to resolve it (page 10). Verdicts: Holds = supports the hypothesis; Unproven = evidence inconclusive; Fails: refine = hypothesis needs refining

lead_message.text: C's 8% margin is an allocation effect: only $0.4M of its $3.3M allocated cost is avoidable, against $3.8M of contribution

slides.rationale: Walk from sales to reported profit, separating avoidable from stranded cost -> waterfall
slides.unit_line: **Connector C, walk from sales to reported profit**, $ millions, FY2026

sidebar.caption: a year of profit lost if C exits, before any migration: the decision-relevant figure, not 8%
bullets: **Two different margins:** reported margin = (6.0 − 2.2 − 3.3) ÷ 6.0 = 8.3%; contribution margin = 3.8 ÷ 6.0 = 63.3%
**88% of the allocation stays:** $2.9M of the $3.3M is shared regulatory documentation and plant depreciation, spread by historical engineering hours
**The dashboard label misleads:** "product gross margin" is measured after shared allocations, so it cannot rank products for an exit or capacity decision

footnotes: Direct contribution $3.8M = 63% of sales; reported profit $0.5M = 8.3%. Avoidable fixed cost $0.40M a year per Finance; variable cost fully avoidable

lead_message.text: On contribution C is the strongest connector, 63% against D's 50%, and its exit would strand $2.9M of cost on A, B and D

slides.rationale: Two sides of one point: margin ranking flips on contribution; exit pushes stranded cost onto the rest -> two panels, no arrow

panels.header: On contribution margin C ranks first; on reported margin it ranks last
If C exits, the stranded cost lands on A, B and D, and B's reported margin falls to about 17%
panels.unit_line: **Reported margin if C exits**, illustrative, % of sales, once $2.9M is reallocated pro rata

slides.so_what: The same margin-ranking logic would then pick B as the next "weakest" product, while total allocated cost falls by only $0.4M, from $6.5M to $6.1M
footnotes: Contribution margin = (sales − variable) ÷ sales; reported = (sales − variable − allocated) ÷ sales. In dollars A's $7.0M contribution is largest; C's $3.8M equals B's
Pack gives no split of the stranded cost; assumed pro rata (1.2 : 1.2 : 0.8): A and B $1.20M → $2.29M each, D $0.80M → $1.53M. D includes $1.5M migrated revenue at 50%

lead_message.text: Exiting C costs $4.75M of cash contribution in year one and $2.65M a year after, even if D wins the optimistic 25%

slides.rationale: Recurring bridge, one-time penalty and the effect on operating profit prove one claim -> three panels, no arrows

panels.header: Every year: exit loses $2.65M even with D migration at its ceiling
panels.unit_line: **Recurring annual impact of exit** against retaining C, $M

panels.header: Year one: one-time penalties deepen the loss to $4.75M
panels.unit_line: **First 12 months after exit** against retaining C, $M

panels.header: Operating profit falls 26%, or 34% with no migration

slides.so_what: Penalties are one-time: even with every penalty waived, exit still loses $2.65M a year
footnotes: 25% of C revenue is a ceiling from three sales interviews, not a forecast; it needs customer-specific adapters and validation. Not yet costed: requalification, clinical documentation, lost A/B accounts
Penalty is first-year only, per Finance. Operating profit = contribution 16.6 − fixed 6.5; exit: (16.6 − 3.8 + 0.75) − (6.5 − 0.4)

lead_message.text: No migration rate makes exit pay: even full migration to D still loses $0.4M a year, and D can absorb only 25% today
highlights: All of C ($6.0M of D sales)

slides.rationale: Impact across migration shares -> columns by share, the full-migration bar highlighted
slides.unit_line: **Recurring annual impact of exit, by share of C revenue migrating to D**, $M; impact = −3.8 + 0.4 + (share × $6.0M × 50%)

sidebar.caption: of migrated D revenue needed to offset the $3.4M lost each year ($3.4M ÷ 50%): 113% of C's entire $6.0M revenue and 4.5 times D's spare capacity
bullets: **Why D cannot close the gap:** C's 63% contribution margin is higher than D's incremental 50%, so each dollar moved from C to D earns less
**Migration crowds out D growth:** the 25% ceiling would use all of D's $1.5M spare capacity, leaving no room for D's own organic growth
**The 25% is unobserved:** it is the portfolio team's ceiling from three interviews; Finance has not estimated any recapture beyond it

categories: All of C ($6.0M of D sales)
highlight: All of C ($6.0M of D sales)

footnotes: Shares above 25% are hypothetical: they exceed D's current capacity and would need new D capacity and a validated adapter at every account. Excludes the one-time $2.1M penalty

lead_message.text: Redeploying to D cannot replace C, because D's spare capacity caps the gain at $0.75M a year, available even if C stays
highlights: Most D can add at present capacity ($1.5M revenue × 50%)

slides.rationale: What exit gives up against the most D can add -> two bars, D highlighted

sidebar.caption: C's economics compared with the most D can add without new capacity
bullets: **Known:** D has room for $1.5M more revenue whether or not C exits; migrating C customers would fill it and crowd out D's own growth
**Known:** the redesign needs one design team for about four months, then hands it back; **not known:** what those months cost, which we do not invent
**Illustrative ceiling:** a full four-month delay to D would cost at most 4/12 × $0.75M ≈ $0.25M, against $1.25M a year of savings
**Redeploy to D?** Yes, in sequence: C redesign March to June 2027, then D adapter validation and growth from July

lead_message.text: The renewal gap does not show C causes churn: size, legacy equipment and coverage confound it, and it is untested

slides.rationale: Claim, the confounders it ignores, and the test to require -> three columns, the test emphasised

columns.header: The claim: accounts that buy C renew less often, so C causes it
detail: The CEO reads a scatter of hospital renewal rates by product mix as C causing dissatisfaction
Correlation, not causation: C accounts differ systematically from the rest
No counterfactual: no before/after evidence that removing C raises retention
It cannot support exit, and it cannot rule out a C effect either

columns.header: Three factors the comparison does not control for
detail: Smaller hospitals on legacy equipment (named in the briefing pack)
Lower customer-success coverage (named in the briefing pack)
Bundle fill of 91% at the nine C-bundle customers, caused by A/B misses: a further plausible confounder (our hypothesis, untested; the pack does not link it to renewals)
Each of these could lower renewal on its own

columns.header: Tests to run before the Q4 2028 gate
detail: Compare renewal within matched segments (size × equipment age × customer-success coverage)
Control for the bundle fill each account actually received
Code lost-account exit reasons for any mention of C
Track retention of any accounts that drop C or move to D
Only a gap that persists within segments feeds the sunset decision, valued against the $3.4M a year C contributes

lead_message.text: The real service problem is bundle fill at 91% against a 95% contract, caused by A and B misses an exit would not fix
highlights: Contracted bundle fill (actual, nine bundle customers)

slides.rationale: Two definitions of fill against the contract minimum -> two columns with a benchmark line
slides.unit_line: **Two fill-rate measures**, %, FY2026; dashed line = contract minimum

sidebar.header: Fix the measure and the A/B misses, not C
bullets: **The dashboard's 98%** counts C as filled even when the bundle ships late because A or B is missing; the contract measures complete bundles
**Redefine the KPI:** bundle-level contracted fill becomes the headline service metric for every bundle customer; product-level fill only a diagnostic
**Root-cause the A and B misses** on the nine bundle accounts, size buffer stock or allocation priority, and report monthly to the board until fill holds at 95% or above for two consecutive quarters
**Unknown: recovery speed.** The pack gives no timeline or cost; Q3 2027 is a working target for Operations to confirm in February

footnotes: The cause sits in A and B, not C: exiting C leaves the A/B misses in place and makes the nine C-bundles incomplete. Bundle fill is 4 percentage points below the contract minimum

units.text: Do not discontinue C in 2027; redesign C, fix bundle service, and make any sunset a 2029 decision on evidence
C's 8% margin comes from the allocation; C earns $3.8M direct contribution, a 63% contribution margin vs 50% for D and A and 42% for B
Only $0.4M of C's $3.3M allocated cost is avoidable; $2.9M (88%) stays and moves onto A, B and D
Exiting C gives up a net $3.4M a year before any migration; the dashboard 'gross margin' is after allocations and cannot rank products for exit
If C exits, stranded cost lands on A, B and D (pro rata assumption): B's reported margin falls to ~17% and B becomes the next 'weakest'; total allocated cost falls only $0.4M
Exit cuts cash contribution by $4.75M in year one and $2.65M every year after, even at the optimistic 25% migration; operating profit falls 26% (34% with no migration)

25% migration is an optimistic ceiling from three sales interviews, not a forecast; penalties are one-time per Finance; replacement qualification, clinical documentation and lost A/B accounts not yet costed
No migration rate makes exit pay: full migration still loses $0.4M a year; break-even needs $6.8M of D revenue, 113% of C and 4.5x D spare capacity
A 2027 exit breaks the non-negotiables: $2.1M penalty is 2.3x the $0.9M envelope; C in 9 of 14 major bundles; no validated substitute; fill already 91%; needs consent of 9 customers
D's spare capacity caps the upside at $0.75M a year, capturable without exiting C; C's economics are 4.5x that; D's 50% incremental contribution is below C's 63%; growth is not replacement
Redeploy the team to D in sequence: C redesign Mar–Jun 2027, then D from July; engineering opportunity cost not quantified, illustrative ceiling ~$0.25M
The 9-percentage-point renewal gap is correlational and confounded (size, legacy equipment, CS coverage, plausibly bundle fill); no before/after test; cannot support exit nor rule out a C effect
Tests before the Q4 2028 gate (matched segments, control for fill, exit reasons, retention of accounts moving to D); only a within-segment gap feeds the sunset decision, valued against $3.4M a year
Bundle fill is 91% vs 95% contracted; the C dashboard's 98% excludes A/B bundle misses; the cause is A and B, so exiting C would not fix it
Redefine the KPI to bundle-level fill, root-cause A/B misses, report monthly until ≥95% for two quarters; recovery speed unknown, Q3 2027 working target
Redesign is the only option that adds value and meets every constraint: +$2.4M (2.37) over 2027–29 vs −$8.7M (−8.73, −10.6 no migration) for exit; retain and delayed sunset 0
Retain unchanged: price pressure erodes C and the $1.25M saving is forgone; delayed 2029 sunset without redesign locks in high-cost C; exit risks A/B bundle volume and makes B next weakest
The $0.55M redesign pays back in ~5 months; breaks even at 19% of the $1.25M estimate (31% if full $0.9M spent); downside (half savings, 3 months late, $0.9M) still +$0.40M
Redesign lifts C's reported margin to ~29% (level with D's 30%) and operating profit 12% to $11.35M; caution: $1.25M is 57% of C's direct cost, tested by the two-site pilot
Use the two renewals to keep C, give no exit notice, add a consent-based D substitution clause and align term end with 2029 expiries
Other seven bundle customers: confirm supply, pre-notify the design change; carry the $2.1M as a contingent one-time liability; run D adapter qualification from Jul 2027; leads proposed
Gate 1, end Aug 2027: convert the whole line only if pilot run-rate saving ≥$0.4M a year and no requalification failed; otherwise stop at pilot sites within $0.9M

Gate 2, Q4 2028 (or notice deadline): sunset only if adapter validated on every hospital model, acceptance high enough, D capacity in place, fill ≥95% for 2 quarters, renewal gap causal, exit bridge positive
None of the open unknowns is likely to flip the decision against exit; each is tested at a gate, incl. C price pressure (exit breaks even only if C contribution falls ~70% to $1.15M)
Six decisions for the February 2027 board: reject exit, approve $0.55M + $0.35M reserve, mandate bundle KPI, authorise renewal terms, sequence engineering, set Gate 2 criteria
Key assumptions: FY2026 volumes hold; penalty payable unless consent; $0.4M is Finance's estimate; undiscounted three-year horizon; penalty counted against the cash envelope
Eight judgement calls where the pack was silent, each conservative or answer-neutral
Calculation log of every number from briefing-pack inputs
Hypothesis test: 'keep C' survived four of five tests; the fifth showed keeping C unchanged is not enough

check.notes: Read unit by unit against the slides: same numbers, conditions, ranking of options and gates; slide order 1–19 kept. Every number traced to the briefing pack or recomputed from it; no corrections needed. Wording clarified, not changed: exec item 1 says 'on contribution margin ... strongest' (source: 'highest-contribution'), since in dollars A's $7.0M is larger; slide 5 footnote says so. Slide 6 shown as three panels because the renderer's waterfall has no subtotals; slide 8 shown as four pillars and slide 17 as six tiles instead of tables/lists; slide 13's three KPI tiles folded into a sidebar.
